Project Description: Assess, redesign, and implement Unifi and Palo Alto firewalls with SD-WAN architecture across HQ and 20 remote campus sites.
PSM Project Description:
Found it in my spam.  Whitelisted and accepted ?.

 

Attached are those PDFs.  The Big Picture one is probably more useful to you, as it has an example of a typical camp setup, as well as a zoomed-out version of the Service Center (what we call our headquarters, usually shortened to “SC”).  The other map is a more detailed map of the SC.  We have two buildings in the SC, 420 and 540.  The PA220 in 540 isn’t really used.  So, that part of the map isn’t completely up to date, but the rest of the maps I just made sure are up to date.  Camps are using Unifi UXG Pro firewalls, except for one with a UDM Pro.  We want to use Unifi Site Magic SD-WAN to connect all camps to the Service Center by adding a UXG Pro in the SC.  I’ve added the UXG Pro to the “little” network map the way it is currently wired up, though I have the ports disabled on it, since it isn’t set up.

 

Currently, we are using IPSec tunnels from camps to the SC.  Some camps have dynamic public IPs and some don’t even have public IPs (CG-NAT).  Only one WAN at the camp is used for the tunnels.  So, if that goes down, their tunnel goes down.  Also, at the SC, the Palo Altos take a while to bring up the tunnels on the secondary firewall, when that gets flipped (most often seen during firmware updates).  Moving to the SD-WAN has a few goals:

More reliable HA tunnels
Simpler tunnel setup
Remove need for DDNS for tunnels
 

A big reason I want aid in this project is that we are dealing with the firewalls used in prod in the headquarters (SC), and the person that originally configured the Palo Altos is no longer here.  Some configs I don’t understand, and our lab environment for testing out this sort of thing isn’t set up yet.  The biggest “?” in the configs for me is why some subnets are declared in the Palo Alto, while others are relying on static routes.
